newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian air traffic controllers call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Italian air traffic controllers call off strike.

text.p: Italian air traffic controllers called off plans for an eight-hour national strike on Wednesday following last minute talks with the government.
The air traffic controllers' unions said they cancelled the stoppage after an accord was signed in the presence of Transport Minister Claudio Burlando.
The agreement set the terms for a future meeting between the parties to settle long-running contract disputes which have brought air services to a standstill in a string of stoppages this year.
The national flag carrier Alitalia said in a statement normal services would resume on Thursday after flights were cut in anticipation of the planned strike.

It was not clear whether a further air traffic controller stoppage planned for May 30 would now go ahead. Air travel is just one of the many transport sectors to be hit by a wave of strikes this year.

Local public transport unions called a one-day national strike earlier this week which forced commuters in Rome and other big centres to find alternative means of transport. Some railway unions plan industrial action for June 1.
Ferry pilots' unions were also on strike on Wednesday.
